originality.rationale: The exact qubit formula alone shares a Fourier strategy with a published scalar result for sign-only steps. The combined first-dimension separation for the ternary metric-cotype test is not implied by that Hilbert argument or by the new general Schatten trace-class upper bound: a non-Hilbert three-outcome 4-cycle gives ratio 5 while all qubit maps obey 9/2. Actual primary and public-result comparisons found no stated equivalent quantitative dimension threshold; unindexed historical calculations remain possible.

value.rationale: The 2026 general S1 metric-cotype theorem leaves finite-dimensional sharp constants unknown. The new theorem fully classifies all qubit constants across all even torus scales, dimensions and Schatten exponents, while proving that the same sharp qubit inequality already fails for classical three-outcome states on the smallest two-dimensional even torus. This is a motivated threshold distinguishing Hilbertian Bloch-ball distance from trace-distance simplex geometry, not an arbitrary finite recomputation; the qutrit bound is explicitly not claimed sharp.
